# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**On settlements vs roads:** Always build settlements when you have the resources. Settlements are worth 3 points while roads are worth 1 point. The value difference is too large to ignore. Build a settlement whenever you can afford it, even if it leaves you without optimal resources for the next round.

**On trading in early rounds:** When you have a balanced hand that lets you build a settlement immediately, do not trade. Post no offer. Your balanced holdings are more valuable than any trade you can make in early rounds. Lock in your 3-point building opportunity before considering what others might need.

**On trading in middle rounds:** Evaluate whether any trade materially improves your path to building. If you're already behind on points, be willing to trade to catch up. If you're even or ahead, only trade if it's clearly in your favor. Trading with resource-rich opponents to strengthen them further is generally a losing move.

**On the final round:** With no future rounds ahead, maximize your score with what you have. Building is always better than holding. If you can build a settlement, build it. Do not avoid building in the final round for any reason related to positioning or future strategy.

**On offerings generally:** When in doubt about whether to post an offer, post none. Offering gives away information and creates opportunities for opponents without clear reciprocal benefit to you. Make your offers count for something concrete, not just to stay active.

**On being tied for the lead:** Don't play conservatively just because you're tied. The game ends in one round, so close is close. Build what you can. Getting 9 points while tied means you got outpaced by someone else who also got 9 or more.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**Opening strategy:** Always build a settlement in round 1 if you have the resources (1 of each). Settlements are worth 3 points versus 1 for roads, and early scoring compounds your advantage.

**Trading philosophy:** Only trade when you cannot build with current resources. Avoid giving up resources that unlock building opportunities unless you get something that enables an immediate, higher-value build.

**Identify your excess resource:** After each yield phase, note which resource you have in surplus (like my 2 ore early on). This is your trading currency, but don't trade it away unless it directly advances your position.

**Build prioritization:** Always choose settlement over road when you have the choice. A settlement's 3-point swing is worth pursuing even if it requires negotiation.

**Late-game pressure:** In the final rounds, assess whether you can build a settlement. If you can, pursue it aggressively through trading if necessary. A settlement in round 5 is worth more than any unopened opportunities.

**When you're blocked:** If you lack a critical resource for building (like I lacked wood in round 4), immediately flag that as your trading target for the next round. Don't wait for the next yield phase hoping luck will help.

**Competitive trading:** Be cautious about trading with players ahead of you in points—trades that strengthen leaders hurt you twice. When trading, prefer partners who are already losing rather than those who are winning.

**Accept good offers immediately:** If an offer lets you build on your next turn, accept it. Don't hold out for better trades that may not materialize.

**What did not work:** Trying to position myself strategically by offering trades to the player in last place (P2) while weakening the leader (P0) was ineffective. I should have focused purely on whether trades unblock my own builds, not on blocking others.

# Playbook for ref_exchange__shipped

**Early rounds: prioritize high-value builds**
When I have the resources to build a settlement, build it immediately. Settlements are worth 3 points versus 1 for roads, and securing points early gives me a lead that compounds across rounds.

**Trading: be strategic about what you offer**
When I post an offer, ensure it genuinely helps me move toward a buildable state (having 1 of each resource for a settlement or 1 wood + 1 brick for a road). Do not make trades just to move resources around without a clear path to building.

**Recognize when you're in a weak position**
If I enter a late round with imbalanced holdings (e.g., 1 ore and nothing else), acknowledge that I've already made suboptimal trades earlier and cannot recover. Do not waste late-round efforts on trades that won't let me build.

**Trading: consider blocking strategically but don't overcommit to it**
When tied or behind a competitor, I can consider trades that deny them resources. However, denying an opponent's build is only valuable if I can simultaneously improve my own position. Never make a trade purely to block if it leaves me unable to build.

**When you receive an offer**
Before declining an offer I cannot fulfill, double-check my holdings. More importantly, before reaching that point, never post an offer that requires resources from me that I don't actually have.

**Late game with insufficient resources**
When I have fewer than 4 resources in the final round and cannot build, accept this is the outcome of earlier decisions. Do not attempt trades that won't complete a buildable set.
